formulas.formula: Payday to payday, in pounds. Bills, budget, savings and your ISA allowance, all in one place.
1. Setup: your payday. Your budget runs payday to payday, the way most of us actually live (weekend paydays move to the Friday).
2. Income: your take-home pay and anything else that comes in each month.
3. Bills: your direct debits and standing orders, with the date each one comes out.
4. Budget: plan each category for one pay month. Spent fills in from Transactions.
5. Transactions: log what you spend. Pick a category from the list.
6. Savings & ISA: balances, and how much of this tax year's ISA allowance you've used.
7. Dashboard and Monthly: how this pay month and the whole year are going.
Your 'month' starts on payday. No more 'where did it go' in the last week.
Each tax year (6 April to 5 April) you can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs. Unused allowance doesn't roll over.
Up to £4,000 a year, with a 25% government bonus. Great for a first home.
Usually 10 monthly payments. You can ask to spread it over 12.
Clear the white cells on Income, Bills, Budget, Transactions and Savings & ISA, then update Setup.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Green: on track, or money left.
Red: over budget, over the allowance, or something to check.
